    "sheet": "Settings",
    "cell": "O45",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Exclude under the pure prediction/descriptive exclusion in the supplied instructions. Figure 1 and Table 5, Section 4.3, pp. 383,391-394: High-minus-low returns summarize portfolios selected by valuation signals. High/low decile membership is not treatment assignment. Comparing FM and BM predictive premia does not by itself establish a causal setting. The paper provides an economic explanation for the apparent premium decline, but does not interpret these signal coefficients as effects of changing X on Y. This decision is about interpretation, not the absence of randomization or remaining endogeneity."

    "after": "Observational linear interaction design, not an implemented treated/post parallel-trends DiD or a local-polynomial RD. EPS proximity and covenant threshold do not themselves make this RD. Breach×STLender measures differential breach-associated outcome for short-termist lenders, not an IV effect of actual enforcement. Authors acknowledge omitted unobservables and manipulation pp.3476,3484. Identifying FE, not HDFE: source reports Quarter, Industry×Quarter, Lender and Lender×Quarter rows cumulatively. Quarter is nested in Industry×Quarter; Lender is additionally nested in Lender×Quarter. Effective sets by baseline column: (1) quarter; (2) industry×quarter; (3) industry×quarter + lender; (4–5) industry×quarter + lender×quarter. Equation3 itself writes only the two interacted sets. Explicit pp3482–3483 discussion addresses confounding. Preserve every reported Yes/No row as source reporting, but do not count redundant sets as extra separately absorbed dimensions. Analogous year nesting applies to TableB.7. Routine FE/control variants at this table are grouped after nested-FE adjudication; no additional HDFE method is established. Source: Breach×STLender on probability of at least20% quarterly total investment decline; Table12B columns1–5, all identifying-FE/control variants.. Publisher Internet Appendix Table IA1 caption (printed p.21/PDF22) specifies joint significance tests of moderator × Chebyshev interaction terms, with the moderator also included in levels. These are not Wald/local-Wald treatment-effect estimators, and the printed baseline coefficient block is not a table of each augmented specification’s full coefficients. Several reported Wald values are negative with p=1.000; retain the source inconsistency without treating those entries as valid conventional nonnegative Wald statistics or repairing them. Source: AppendixA1 pp.34,36,38; TableIA1 Wald(intl), printed pp.21–35.. Source link: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2023.07.002."
  }
]

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.9; expected GDP growth. Table OA.9: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yields IV. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield on disagreement about infla- tion (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected GDP growth (ExpGDP). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpGDP is the annualized pre- dictor of the mean of GDP growth over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 1y         2y     3y   4y       5y        1y     2y     3y    4y     5y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.10; ExpCII forecast from lagged consumption growth. Table OA.10: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yields V. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected con- sumption growth (ExpCII ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCII is the annualized esti- mator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a constant and current quarterly consumption growth. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters         Surveys of Consumers Maturity 1y         2y    3y    4y       5y        1y     2y     3y    4y    5y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.11; ExpCIII forecast adding disagreement. Table OA.11: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yields VI. The table reports re- sults from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and ex- pected consumption growth (ExpCIII ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annual- ized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCIII is the annualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a con- stant, current quarterly consumption growth, and current inflation disagreement. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 1y       2y     3y     4y       5y       1y    2y     3y    4y     5y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.12; ExpCIV forecast adding inflation. Table OA.12: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yields VII. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and ex- pected consumption growth (ExpCIV ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annual- ized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCIV is the an- nualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a constant, current quarterly consumption growth, current inflation disagreement, and current quarterly inflation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 1y       2y     3y     4y       5y       1y    2y     3y    4y     5y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.13; ExpCV forecast with instrumented real-yield predictor. Table OA.13: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yields VIII. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and ex- pected consumption growth (ExpCV ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annual- ized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCV is the an- nualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a constant, current quarterly consumption growth, current inflation disagreement, and the instrumented two year real yield. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 1y       2y     3y     4y       5y       1y    2y     3y    4y     5y"

    "before": null,
    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.16; expected GDP growth. Table OA.16: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yields III. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected GDP growth (ExpGDP). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpGDP is the annualized predictor of the mean of GDP growth over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 2y          3y     5y    7y      10y      2y    3y     5y      7y 10y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.17; ExpCII. Table OA.17: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yields IV. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected consumption growth (ExpCII ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCII is the annualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a constant and current quarterly consumption growth. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 2y         3y    5y     7y      10y      2y     3y     5y      7y 10y"

    "before": null,
    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.18; ExpCIII. Table OA.18: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yields V. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected consumption growth (ExpCIII ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annual- ized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCIII is the annualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a con- stant, current quarterly consumption growth, and current inflation disagreement. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 2y        3y    5y     7y      10y       2y    3y     5y      7y 10y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.19; ExpCIV. Table OA.19: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yields VI. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected consumption growth (ExpCIV ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCIV is the annualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a constant, current quarterly consumption growth, current inflation disagreement, and current quarterly inflation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters       Surveys of Consumers Maturity 2y        3y    5y     7y      10y      2y     3y     5y      7y 10y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.20; ExpCV. Table OA.20: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yields VII. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and expected consumption growth (ExpCV ). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpCV is the annualized estimator from a regression of future quarterly consumption growth on a constant, current quarterly consumption growth, current inflation disagreement, and the instrumented two year real yield. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity 2y         3y    5y     7y      10y       2y    3y     5y      7y 10y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.24; GDP-growth volatility. Table OA.24: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yield Volatilities IV. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield volatility on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and the volatility of GDP growth (SigGDP). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey- West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. SigGDP is the annualized predictor of the volatility of GDP growth over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers Maturity     1y      2y    3y     4y     5y       1y     2y     3y    4y     5y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.25; consumption-growth mean and volatility. Table OA.25: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yield Volatilities V. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield volatility on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), expected consumption growth (ExpC), and the volatility of consumption growth (SigC). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression co- efficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpC and SigC are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of consumption growth over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters    Surveys of Consumers"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.26; VXO uncertainty. Table OA.26: Inflation Disagreement and Nominal Yield Volatilities VI. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the one-, to five-year nominal yield volatility on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), the volatility of consumption growth (SigC), and the CME Volatility Index VXO. The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. The VXO volatility index is based on trading of S&P 100 (OEX) options. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q2-1986 to Q2-2014.     "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.29; GDP-growth volatility. Table OA.29: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yield Volatilities III. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield volatility on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatil- ity of inflation (SigInf), and GDP growth volatility (SigGDP). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the correspond- ing yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. SigGDP is the annualized predictor of the volatility of consumption growth over the cor- responding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters      Surveys of Consumers Maturity 2y         3y   5y      7y      10y    2y     3y      5y     7y    10y"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.30; consumption-growth mean and volatility. Table OA.30: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yield Volatilities IV. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield volatility on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatil- ity of inflation (SigInf), expected consumption growth (ExpC), and consumption growth volatility (SigC). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags and regres- sion coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. ExpC and SigC are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of consumption growth over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q3-1981 to Q2-2014. Survey of Professional Forecasters        Surveys of Consumers"

    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.31; VXO uncertainty. Table OA.31: Inflation Disagreement and Real Yield Volatilities V. The table reports results from OLS regressions of the two, three, five, seven, and ten-year real yield volatility on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), the volatility of inflation (SigInf), and the CME Volatility Index VXO. The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey- West corrected with 12 lags and regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are annualized predictors of the mean and volatility of inflation over the corresponding yield maturity horizon using a GARCH(1,1) model with an ARMA(1,1) mean equation. The VXO volatility index is based on trading of S&P 100 (OEX) options. Data are available at the quarterly frequency from Q2-1986 to Q2-2014.   {
    "sheet": "Settings",
    "cell": "N2224",
    "before": null,
    "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.32; GSW nominal yields, SPF. Table OA.32: SPF Inflation Disagreement and Gürkaynak, Sack and Wright (2010) Nominal Yields. The table reports results from OLS regressions of nominal yields and their volatilities on disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), and the volatility of inflation (SigInf). Monthly nominal discount bond yields are from Gürkaynak, Sack and Wright (2010). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags. Regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are predicted by a GARCH(1, 1) model with an ARMA(1, 1) mean equation over multiple horizons (T). Sample: Q3-1981 to Q2-2014.     "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.35; real-yield proxy subtracting VAR expected inflation. Table OA.35: Real Yields = Nominal Yields - Expected Inflation from VAR. The table reports results from OLS regressions of real yields on disagreement about inflation (Dis- Inf) in the top panel and disagreement about inflation (DisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf) and the volatility of inflation (SigInf). Real yields are computed from nominal yields by sub- tracting expected inflation (ExpInf). ExpInf is predicted by regressing realized inflation over the bond maturity horizon on lagged monthly inflation and yields with maturity 1-5 years. The volatility of inflation is calculated by regressing the squared residuals from the first regression onto lagged squared residuals and yields with maturity 1-5 years. The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags. Regression coefficients are standardized. Samples: Q3-1981 to Q2-2014 and January 1978 to June 2014. SPF                              MSC 1y     2y     3y     4y     5y    1y    2y      3y    4y      5y"

Table OA.36: Cross-Sectional Variance as a Measure of Inflation Disagreement. The table reports results from OLS regressions of real and nominal yields and their volatilities on disagreement about inflation (DisInf) and expected inflation (ExpInf). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags. Regression coefficients are standardized. Disagreement about inflation is the cross-sectional variance of one year ahead inflation fore- casts (DisInf). ExpInf is predicted by a GARCH(1, 1) model with an ARMA(1, 1) mean equation over multiple horizons (T). Samples: Q3-1981 to Q2-2014 and January 1978 to June 2014. Table OA.37: Interquartile Range as a Measure of Inflation Disagreement. The table reports results from OLS regressions of real and nominal yields and their volatilities on disagreement about inflation (DisInf) and expected inflation (ExpInf). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags. Regression coefficients are standardized. Disagreement about inflation is the interquartile range (IQR) of one year ahead inflation forecasts (DisInf) computed from the 75th percentile minus the 25th percentile of inflation forecasts. ExpInf is predicted by a GARCH(1, 1) model with an ARMA(1, 1) mean equation over multiple horizons (T). Samples: Q3-1981 to Q2-2014 and January 1978 to June 2014. Table OA.40: Normalized Inflation Disagreement and Real and Nominal Yield Volatilities. The table reports results from OLS regressions of real and nominal yield volatilities on disagreement about inflation scaled by the volatility of inflation (NormDisInf), expected inflation (ExpInf), and the volatility of inflation (SigInf). The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags. Regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf and SigInf are predicted by a GARCH(1, 1) model with an ARMA(1, 1) mean equation over multiple horizons (T). Samples: Q3-1981 to Q2-2014 and January 1978 to June 2014.     "after": "OLS effect of continuous survey inflation disagreement on the grouped outcomes in TableOA.45; real consumption volatility controls. Table OA.45: Real Consumption. The top table reports results from OLS regressions of real yields on disagreement about inflation (DisInf) and real consumption growth volatility (SigC). The bottom table reports results from OLS regressions of nominal yields on disagree- ment about inflation, expected inflation (ExpInfl), and real consumption growth volatility. The t-statistics (t-stat) are Newey-West corrected with 12 lags. Regression coefficients are standardized. ExpInf is predicted by a GARCH(1, 1) model with an ARMA(1, 1) mean equation over multiple horizons (T). SigC is also predicted by a GARCH(1, 1) model with an ARMA(1, 1) mean equation.   {
    "sheet": "Comparisons",
    "cell": "R3491",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. Real-yield prose says positively related and the parameters are introduced as controls. A narrow only-DisInf-as-focal interpretation would omit them, but is inconsistent with accepting nominal ExpInf and GDP-disagreement controls on comparably broad contextual evidence. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown."
  },

  {
    "sheet": "Comparisons",
    "cell": "R3551",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. Real-yield prose says positively related and the parameters are introduced as controls. A narrow only-DisInf-as-focal interpretation would omit them, but is inconsistent with accepting nominal ExpInf and GDP-disagreement controls on comparably broad contextual evidence. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown."
  },

    "cell": "R3571",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. The causal statement cites other empirical evidence and is an omitted-variable motivation. The paper does not claim a new robust volatility effect. Broad author-intention rule favors retaining the implemented parameter including null estimates; this is more contestable than nominal expected inflation. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown."

  {
    "sheet": "Comparisons",
    "cell": "R3671",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. The causal statement cites other empirical evidence and is an omitted-variable motivation. The paper does not claim a new robust volatility effect. Broad author-intention rule favors retaining the implemented parameter including null estimates; this is more contestable than nominal expected inflation. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown."
  },

    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. Real-yield prose says positively related and the parameters are introduced as controls. A narrow only-DisInf-as-focal interpretation would omit them, but is inconsistent with accepting nominal ExpInf and GDP-disagreement controls on comparably broad contextual evidence. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown. Caption cites GSW2010 although main text cites GSW2007; preserve provenance conflict."

    "sheet": "Comparisons",
    "cell": "R3766",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. Real-yield prose says positively related and the parameters are introduced as controls. A narrow only-DisInf-as-focal interpretation would omit them, but is inconsistent with accepting nominal ExpInf and GDP-disagreement controls on comparably broad contextual evidence. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown. Caption cites GSW2010 although main text cites GSW2007; preserve provenance conflict."
  },

  {
    "sheet": "Comparisons",
    "cell": "R3801",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. Real-yield prose says positively related and the parameters are introduced as controls. A narrow only-DisInf-as-focal interpretation would omit them, but is inconsistent with accepting nominal ExpInf and GDP-disagreement controls on comparably broad contextual evidence. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown."
  },

  {
    "sheet": "Comparisons",
    "cell": "R3896",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-interpretation gate is a moderate judgment, not identification endorsement. Real-yield prose says positively related and the parameters are introduced as controls. A narrow only-DisInf-as-focal interpretation would omit them, but is inconsistent with accepting nominal ExpInf and GDP-disagreement controls on comparably broad contextual evidence. Continuous observational target/weights not separately established; same regression sample does not prove causal SD alignment, hence unknown."
  },

  {
    "sheet": "Settings",
    "cell": "O2321",
    "before": null,
    "after": "Author-explicit forecast-rule counterfactual, not causal effect of short interest on prices: §4 says the investor uses the alternative forecast instead, and footnote29 holds the ten-year variance forecast fixed so weights differ only because of return forecasts. Same realized underlying market/bill path, weights recomputed, price-taking interpretation; no transaction-cost, loan-fee or market-impact adjustment established. Nonlinear performance recomputation, not OLS. Binary refers to implemented rule-versus-prevailing-mean contrast, not continuously varying SII/weights. Review this inclusion priority independently. Supporting competing-rule results explicitly implemented and discussed, not merely predictive-regression coefficient rows. Source: §4 pp57–59, Table7 TMS row (PDF12–14)."
  }
]
